title: Magnitude 5.9 Earthquake Rattles Tokyo and Kanto Region, No Tsunami Warning
excerpt: The quake struck southern Ibaraki Prefecture early Sunday morning, shaking buildings across the greater Tokyo area and injuring several people.
body:
• A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Toride in Ibaraki Prefecture at 2:00 AM local time Sunday, shaking the greater Tokyo area
  • The Japan Meteorological Agency recorded seismic intensity of lower-5 in some areas — strong enough to rattle furniture and crack walls
  • No tsunami warning was issued; nuclear plants at Tokai, Fukushima Daiichi, and Fukushima Daini reported no abnormalities
  • Several people were injured across the Kanto region, with reports from Kawasaki and Saitama

A magnitude 5.9 earthquake shook Japan's Kanto region early Sunday morning, jolting residents of Tokyo and surrounding prefectures awake and prompting the government to set up an emergency liaison office at the Prime Minister's residence.

The quake struck at 2:00 AM local time on August 23 with its epicenter near Toride in southern Ibaraki Prefecture, about 40 kilometers northeast of central Tokyo. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded the magnitude at 5.8, while the Japan Meteorological Agency measured it at 5.9 with a depth of approximately 60 to 70 kilometers.

Strong Shaking Across the Capital Region

The JMA recorded seismic intensity of shindo lower-5 — a level that causes unsecured furniture to move, cracks to appear in walls, and difficulty standing — in parts of Ibaraki and neighboring prefectures. Shaking was felt across the entire Kanto region, including Ibaraki, Saitama, Chiba, and Tokyo.

More than 360 people reported feeling the earthquake through the USGS felt-report system within hours of the event. A 3.2 magnitude aftershock followed five minutes later in southern Ibaraki.

Several people were injured across the region. Three people sustained minor injuries in Kawasaki and two in Saitama. In Sagamihara, a woman in her 60s fell down stairs during the shaking. None of the injuries were life-threatening, authorities said.

Nuclear Plants Report No Issues

The JMA confirmed there was no tsunami risk from the earthquake. Tokyo Electric Power Company said its Fukushima Daiichi and Fukushima Daini nuclear power plants showed no abnormalities, and radiation levels remained normal. The Tokai 2 nuclear plant in Ibaraki also reported no irregularities.

Prime Minister's office instructed authorities to assess damage and monitor the situation. The government set up a liaison room at the Prime Minister's residence to coordinate the response.

An Active Seismic Period

The earthquake adds to a pattern of heightened seismic activity across Japan this summer. A devastating magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck Kumamoto in southern Japan on July 28, killing dozens and triggering an explosion at a shopping mall. A magnitude 6.9 earthquake hit off the coast near Hachinohe in late June.

The Kanto region sits atop one of the world's most complex tectonic zones, where three tectonic plates converge. Tokyo experiences regular moderate earthquakes, but the shindo lower-5 intensity recorded in this event is strong enough to cause minor structural damage and disrupt daily life.

Residents in the affected areas have been advised to remain alert for possible aftershocks over the coming days. The JMA said earthquakes producing shaking of similar intensity remain possible in the near term and urged caution near steep terrain and older structures.
